query: The (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy provides a large caloric response under applied-field and pressure-field operation but has poor integrity and tends to crack. Prior studies on related MM′X materials used epoxy-containing Mn0.98CoGe, obtaining compressive strengths of 152 and 218 MPa at two epoxy contents, and low-melting In composites, obtaining 48 MPa compressive strength and more than eight times the thermal conductivity of epoxy-containing samples under the reported conditions. These routes demonstrated gains in selected strength or heat-transport metrics, but the desired coexistence of robust integrity and high caloric performance remains unresolved. The target should also remain rare-earth-free. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing caloric response? Present one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, quantitative or directional outcomes relative to the unchanged alloy, boundary conditions under applied-field, pressure, temperature, and loading regimes, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive controlled experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Adding a low volume fraction (~3 vol%) of Al2O3 nanoparticles into the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 high-entropy alloy will bolster the mechanical integrity by refining the microstructure and impeding crack propagation while preserving its large caloric response.
generation.material_initial_state: (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy that exhibits significant caloric effects under applied magnetic and pressure fields but suffers from poor structural integrity and cracking.
generation.intervention: Introduce approximately 3 vol% of Al2O3 nanoparticles into the alloy during synthesis (via, e.g., mechanical alloying followed by consolidation) to form a composite.
generation.conditions: The material is subjected to operational conditions involving applied-field (magnetic or pressure) cycling, room to moderately elevated temperatures, and uniaxial mechanical loading at rates similar to prior epoxy/In composite tests.
generation.structural_mediator: Uniformly dispersed Al2O3 nanoparticles positioned mainly at the grain boundaries, leading to grain refinement and creating effective crack deflection sites.
generation.mechanism: Al2O3 particles exert a Zener pinning effect during solidification and subsequent processing, refining the grain size and acting as barriers to crack propagation. This reinforcement increases compressive strength and ductility while the ceramic phase’s inert nature minimally interacts with the transformation mechanisms responsible for the caloric response.
generation.predicted_outcome: The composite is expected to exhibit approximately a 20% increase in compressive strength and improved crack resistance relative to the unreinforced alloy, yet maintain a caloric response amplitude comparable (within ~10% variation) to that of the pristine material.
generation.baseline: The base (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy without any ceramic reinforcement, which has excellent caloric performance but poor mechanical integrity and a tendency to crack.
generation.boundary: The intervention is applied under similar applied-field and pressure-field conditions as the base alloy; the ceramic content is kept low (<5 vol%) so that the phase transitions underlying the caloric effect are not significantly altered, and tests are conducted at room temperature and moderate working temperatures with comparable loading rates.
generation.uncertainty: It is not entirely clear whether the addition of Al2O3 nanoparticles might slightly alter either the phase transformation kinetics or the field coupling mechanisms that drive the caloric effect. The optimal volume fraction and dispersion stability under repeated cycling also remain to be thoroughly investigated.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy with 3 vol% added Al2O3 nanoparticles and an unreinforced control. Subject both groups to identical applied magnetic/pressure-field cycling and uniaxial compressive loading tests under controlled temperature conditions.
measurements: Fracture toughness or crack propagation behavior
Caloric response amplitude (e.g., temperature change under applied field)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis will be falsified if the Al2O3-reinforced samples do not show a significant improvement (e.g., at least ~20% higher compressive strength or enhanced crack resistance) relative to the control, or if the caloric response amplitude is decreased by more than about 10% compared to the unreinforced alloy.

cited_evidence.text: This work aims to study the influence of Al2O3 in CrFeCuMnNi high-entropy alloy matrix composites (HEMCs) on their microstructure, phase changes, and mechanical and wear performances. CrFeCuMnNi-Al2O3 HEMCs were synthesized via mechanical alloying (MA) followed by hot compaction (550 °C at 550 MPa), medium frequency sintering (1200 °C), and hot forging (1000 °C at 50 MPa). The XRD results demonstrate the formation of both FCC and BCC phases in the synthesized powders, which were transformed into major stable FCC and minor ordered B2-BCC phases, as confirmed by HRSEM. The microstructural variation of HRSEM-EBSD, in terms of the coloured grain map (inverse pole figures), grain size distribution, and misorientation angle, was analysed and reported. The grain size of the matrix decreased with the increase in Al2O3 particles owing to the higher structural refinement by MA and zener pinning of the incorporated Al2O3 particles. The hot-forged CrFeCuMnNi-3 vol.% Al2O3 sample exhibited an ultimate compressive strength of 1.058 GPa, which was 21% higher than that of the unreinforced HEA matrix. AbstractIn order to improve the wear resistance of CoCrNi alloy, TiC was introduced into the alloy and wear-resistant CoCrNi/(TiC)x composites were designed. The effects of TiC contents on the microstructure, mechanical properties, and wear resistance of CoCrNi matrix were investigated, respectively. It was found that the TiC produced dissolution and precipitation process in CoCrNi alloy, and a large number of needled and blocky TiC particles were precipitated in the composites. The compressive yield strength of CoCrNi/(TiC)x composites increased with the increasing TiC content. Compared with the CoCrNi alloy, the yield strength of CoCrNi/(TiC)x composites increased from 108 to 1371 MPa, and the corresponding strengthening mechanism contributed to the second phase strengthening. The wear resistance of CoCrNi/(TiC)x composites was also greatly improved due to the strengthening of TiC. Compared with the CoCrNi alloy, the specific wear rate of CoCrNi/(TiC)1.0 alloy was reduced by about 77%. The wear resistance of CoCrNi/(TiC)x composites was enhanced with the increasing content of TiC addition.Keywords: high-entropy alloy, microstructure, TiC, wear resistance, mechanical properties
